items.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] That's his niece, I think. They were living right there. Yeah. Well, I know the last time I heard Buddy Bolden, Carnish, and the old man who played the bass...

ctx.x: That's his niece, I think. They were living right there. Yeah. Well, I know the last time I heard Buddy Bolden, Carnish, and the old man who played the bass, what is his name again? Bob Lyons. Bob Lyons and this other fellow played guitar, I don't know him. And he was playing in the economy hall, right on the same. What street that you thought where the economy hall was, where the man of them was living?

Not the economy hall. No, the old fellow's hall. No, no, no. You talk about the... Right in that point, the old fellow's hall. No, no, that wasn't the old fellow's hall. That's the hall the chaperon used to take here there. Oh, you're talking about the Creole Hall there.
